pages.quiz:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. How do most flowering plants make new plants? (1 mark)
   A. By walking away
   B. By seeds
   C. By laying eggs
   D. By giving birth

2. What do roots of cassava and sweet potato do besides taking in water? (1 mark)
   A. Carry seeds
   B. Store food
   C. Make leaves
   D. Make flowers

3. Which of these do plants need to stay alive? (1 mark)
   A. Only darkness
   B. Stones and plastic
   C. Water, air and light
   D. Only sand

4. Which of these is a root that we eat? (1 mark)
   A. Maize grain
   B. Cabbage
   C. Banana
   D. Carrot

5. What is the word for the tiny parts in a leaf where air goes in and out? (1 mark)
   A. Roots
   B. Seeds
   C. Petals
   D. Tiny holes

6. What is the main job of leaves? (1 mark)
   A. Holding the plant in the soil
   B. Making food for the plant
   C. Making seeds
   D. Taking in water from the soil

7. Which of these is a safety rule when handling plants? (1 mark)
   A. Pull plants with thorns barehanded
   B. Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   C. Rub sap on your eyes
   D. Taste every fruit you find

8. What does removing waste mean for a plant? (1 mark)
   A. Sending out roots
   B. Cutting its own leaves
   C. Throwing away its seeds
   D. Getting rid of things its body does not need

9. What does a snail do when you touch it? (1 mark)
   A. Flies away
   B. Pulls its body into its shell
   C. Starts to sing
   D. Grows a tail

10. Which animal group breathes using gills? (1 mark)
   A. Fish
   B. Reptiles
   C. Birds
   D. Mammals

11. A tadpole grows into a frog. What does this show? (1 mark)
   A. Only fish grow
   B. Tadpoles are plants
   C. Animals do not grow
   D. Animals grow and change

12. Why is a spider NOT an insect? (1 mark)
   A. It has feathers
   B. It has a backbone
   C. It has eight legs, not six
   D. It lives in water

13. How many legs does an insect have? (1 mark)
   A. Eight
   B. Four
   C. Ten
   D. Six

14. What does the rectum do? (1 mark)
   A. Stores faeces for a short time
   B. Makes saliva
   C. Chews food
   D. Digests proteins

15. Which of these leaves the body through the anus? (1 mark)
   A. Saliva
   B. Stomach juice
   C. Blood
   D. Faeces

16. What is bloating? (1 mark)
   A. A cut in the mouth
   B. Loose faeces
   C. Tiredness
   D. A full, swollen tummy often with gas

17. What does the small intestine mainly absorb? (1 mark)
   A. Digested food
   B. Light
   C. Sound
   D. Air

18. What is constipation? (1 mark)
   A. Having worms
   B. Vomiting
   C. Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty
   D. Passing watery faeces

19. Why is it important to eat slowly? (1 mark)
   A. It stops you growing
   B. It lets you chew well and helps digestion
   C. It makes food taste of salt
   D. It makes you thirsty

20. Which part of the digestive system is long and coiled? (1 mark)
   A. Rectum
   B. Gullet
   C. Small intestine
   D. Mouth

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Give two ways in which animals are different from plants. (2 marks)

22. A pupil pulls up a small bean plant from the garden. Describe what she will see and give the job of each part she sees. (5 marks)

23. Name two roots, two stems and two leaves that people eat. (4 marks)

24. Explain how animals show the signs of life: feeding, growing, and reproducing. Give an example of each. (4 marks)

25. Name the parts of the digestive system in the order food passes through them. (2 marks)

26. Explain why we should wash our hands before eating and after using the toilet. (3 marks)

27. Write three safety rules when observing animals in the school compound. (3 marks)

28. Describe the function of each of these parts of a plant: roots, stem, leaves, flowers. (4 marks)

29. Explain how fibre helps the digestive system. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY — TERMLY EXAM #4 (TERM 1) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. B — By seeds
   Most flowering plants reproduce by making seeds inside fruits.

2. B — Store food
   These roots store food for the plant.

3. C — Water, air and light
   Plants need water, air, light and nutrients from the soil.

4. D — Carrot
   A carrot is a storage root. Cabbage is leaves, banana is a fruit and maize grain is a seed.

5. D — Tiny holes
   Air moves in and out of leaves through tiny holes.

6. B — Making food for the plant
   Leaves use sunlight, water and air to make food.

7. B — Ask an adult before touching a plant you do not know
   Some plants can hurt or poison people, so ask first.

8. D — Getting rid of things its body does not need
   Living things must remove waste made in their bodies.

9. B — Pulls its body into its shell
   This is a response to touch.

10. A — Fish
   Fish take oxygen from water with gills.

11. D — Animals grow and change
   Young animals grow and may change shape as they become adults.

12. C — It has eight legs, not six
   Insects have six legs and spiders have eight.

13. D — Six
   All adult insects have six legs.

14. A — Stores faeces for a short time
   The rectum stores faeces before they pass out.

15. D — Faeces
   Faeces leave the body through the anus.

16. D — A full, swollen tummy often with gas
   Bloating means the tummy feels full and swollen.

17. A — Digested food
   Digested food passes through its wall into blood.

18. C — Passing hard, dry faeces with difficulty
   Constipation means hard faeces that are difficult to pass.

19. B — It lets you chew well and helps digestion
   Chewing well breaks food down before swallowing.

20. C — Small intestine
   The small intestine is a very long coiled tube.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Animals can move from place to place. Animals feed on ready-made food while plants make their own.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct difference.

22. (5 marks)
   Answer: She will see roots that hold the plant and take in water, a stem that holds it up and carries food and water, leaves that make food, and maybe flowers or pods that make seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming each of four parts and 1 mark for correct function overall.

23. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots: carrot, cassava, sweet potato. Stems: sugarcane. Leaves: cabbage, sukuma wiki, spinach (any two of each, with correct grouping).
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct pair and 1 mark for correct grouping overall.

24. (4 marks)
   Answer: Feeding: a goat eats grass. Growing: a chick becomes a hen. Reproducing: a hen lays eggs, or a cow gives birth.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each sign with example, plus 1 mark for explaining growth as getting bigger.

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: Mouth, gullet, stomach, small intestine, large intestine, rectum, anus.
   Working / marking points: Award 2 marks for the correct order. 1 mark if at most two parts are out of order.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: Hands may carry germs and worm eggs. Washing removes them and stops them entering the mouth and causing disease.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for germs on hands, 1 mark for washing removes them, 1 mark for preventing illness.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: Do not pick up animals you do not know, do not harm animals, wash hands after touching soil or animals, return animals to where they were found.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each rule.

28. (4 marks)
   Answer: Roots hold the plant and take in water. The stem supports the plant and carries water and food. Leaves make food. Flowers make fruits and seeds.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct function.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: Fibre in fruits, vegetables and whole grains helps food and waste move through the intestines and helps prevent constipation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for naming fibre foods, 1 mark for movement, 1 mark for constipation.
